statusMeanings.PASS: Every evidence slot the derivation rule requires is present and exists in this tree, and the row carries no evidenceGap. Says nothing about production fitness beyond what the cited evidence covers.
statusMeanings.PARTIAL: The mechanism exists and something in this tree gates it, but at least one required evidence slot is missing or a named gap remains. The gap is always named in evidenceGap.
statusMeanings.FAIL: A user-visible capability is known to be broken, or the evidence needed to claim it is absent while the defect it would have caught has already shipped. A FAIL row is a finding, not a placeholder.
statusMeanings.NOT_APPLICABLE: A decided, recorded exclusion with its reason. Never used for work that is merely unwritten.

derivation.method: Status is derived from what exists in this tree and what the gates actually assert, not from prose. A row is PASS only when every slot below is present AND exists AND evidenceGap is empty; anything else is PARTIAL with the missing slot named, unless a user-visible defect is known, in which case FAIL.
passRequires: oracleFixtures: at least one recording of pinned behaviour that the row's differential compares against
implementation: at least one Go file or package that carries the behaviour
tests: at least one named test that fails when the behaviour is wrong (existence checked, and the name must resolve to a real test function or harness file)
ci: at least one workflow job that runs that test
derivation.productionRule: AGENTS.md 22 and 29-30: a behaviour verified only against our own mock peer is `unverified` for production. Such rows cannot be PASS no matter how complete the fixture is, and the gap says so verbatim.
derivation.artifactRule: AGENTS.md 23 and 34: a release claim needs the shipped artifact, unpacked, started against a stock tree. Rows whose only evidence is the source tree carry that gap until a release-artifact result exists.
derivation.failRule: AGENTS.md 40: a defect that shipped is recorded here even after it is fixed, because the row's status is about the evidence layer that allowed it through. A fixed mechanism promotes a row from FAIL only when the gate that would have caught it exists and has run.

rows.area: Provider transport on the real internet (TLS, proxy, timeouts, decompression, redirects)

wouldGoRedIfWrong.explanation: An untrusted certificate must be refused with an error naming the TLS stage and the provider host and carrying no credential. The row previously had no gate at all for any network failure class; this test plus the DNS, connect and proxy siblings are that gate, and the artifact-level half is TestProviderTransportFailureIsCausalThroughTheShippedBinary.

evidenceGap: THE DEEPSEEK CLAUSE IS NOW RECORDED AS THE DECLARED SUPERSET IT IS. Pinned's catch discards the cause (`{error:true}`), so a causal message there would have been impossible without diverging. GoTavern diverges deliberately and declares it (`internal/server/chat_completions.go:141-154`): `error` stays exactly what pinned sends and a `message` member is added. The artifact test asserts BOTH halves -- the pinned member unchanged and the additive one present -- so the divergence cannot silently become a replacement

STILL OPEN, AND STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: every provider differential in this corpus runs against our own recording peer, and AGENTS.md 22 makes that `unverified` for production purposes. The live canary that reaches a real provider (`scripts/live-canary.mjs`, `scripts/deepseek-canary.mjs`) needs a credential and is not part of the default suite, so "a user's own provider, through a user's own proxy" is exercised by the user and by nothing here
rows.notes: RE-DERIVED 2026-10-29: FAIL -> PARTIAL. The FAIL was for an absent gate: no test asserted a causala error text for a DNS, connect, TLS, proxy or timeout failure while proving no secret was printed, and every measurement came from a recording peer that cannot produce any of those shapes. Four new peers (untrusted certificate, .invalid host, closed port, 407 proxy) plus the pre-existing stalled-peer test are that gate at the transport, and a shipped-binary test asserts the same taxonomy reaches the browser payload with no credential. The row is PARTIAL rather than PASS because the corpus still runs against our own peer and the live canary needs a credential. CLOSED GAPS, moved out of evidenceGap so that field contains only OPEN gaps: CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- THE INTERNET-SHAPED GATE. Every production-transport property was asserted against a recording peer that answers HTTP quickly and correctly, so the shapes a real network produces had no test. `internal/outbound/transport_internet_shape_test.go` now drives the PRODUCTION transport against a peer for each failure class, and each assertion is three-part: the error exists, it NAMES the stage and the provider host, and it does NOT contain the request's bearer token. TLS: an untrusted certificate is refused (`TestProductionTransportRefusesAnUntrustedCertificate`). DNS: the RFC 2606 `.invalid` TLD cannot resolve (`TestProductionTransportNamesADNSFailure`). Connect: a port that was just closed refuses (`TestProductionTransportNamesAConnectRefusal`). Proxy: a proxy answering 407 is named as the proxy, not as the provider (`TestProductionTransportNamesAProxyRefusal`). Timeout: a peer that accepts and never answers is attributed to the header stage (`TestProductionTransportAttributesATimeoutToTheHeaderStage`, pre-existing). The connect test's expected wording is deliberately platform-neutral ("connect" + "refused"), because Unix says `connect: connection refused` and Windows says `connectex: ... actively refused it`, and a host-specific phrase would have made the gate untransportable CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- THROUGH THE SHIPPED ARTIFACT, which is what AGENTS.md 23 and 35 require. `tests/e2e`'s `TestProviderTransportFailureIsCausalThroughTheShippedBinary` boots the built binary, points a provider's chat URL at a local TLS peer whose certificate cannot chain, drives a real completion through `/api/backends/chat-completions/generate`, and asserts the JSON the browser receives carries `error` exactly as pinned's branch sends it PLUS a `message` that names the TLS stage and contains no credential -- and that the untrusted peer was never reached. THE TEETH WERE OBSERVED: removing the `message` member from `pinnedChatCompletionErrorFlagWithCause` turns it red with `the failure body carries no message, so the user sees no cause (this is the P0-A shape): {"error":true}` (exit 1); the byte copy was restored and the test went green CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- THE STALE DOCUMENT. `docs/network-egress.md` §2 presented the pre-split `raw.go` measurements as current and is now restated: a status table maps each of D1-D8 to the implementation and the test that would go red, the old table is kept as HISTORY with a banner saying it is superseded, and a paragraph names what is still NOT proven (the differential corpus still runs against our own recording peer)

rows.area: Streaming SSE framing, incremental render and cancellation

wouldGoRedIfWrong.explanation: the row's claims about streaming sse framing, incremental render and cancellation rest on this test; deleting or weakening it makes the row unsupported, and the checker fails a row whose named test does not exist

rows.notes: Streaming has the deepest browser instrumentation in the tree (frame-by-frame render alignment on both legs). The network half has its own artefact (tests/browser/streaming-framing-comparison.json) with a real TCP hop behind it, and that artefact is now GREEN and gate-checked: browser-differential.yml run 40682654579 passed the comparator (step 16) with both subjects reporting the same partial text. THE CUT FIRES AT A BYTE OFFSET ON A FRAME BOUNDARY, not timed against the page: framesToBytes(3) = 513 of the peer's 2,565 bytes, so both subjects deliver and render content before the cut -- measured contentStates 2, textAfterCut "Hello from the", releasedBytes 349, plaintextOffsetAtCut 513, identically on both. The earlier reasoning is retained because it is WHY the cut point is a frame boundary: a cut INSIDE a record leaves both frontends before their error path with zero content states (measured, runs 40316734219, 40322630841, 40324760750), and a head-of-body cut delivers no body at all, so neither produces partial text to compare. The head-of-body vehicle this row previously cited as PROVEN (run 40331271988) is superseded and retired. Buffering-proxy mode is a DECIDED EXCLUSION, not a gap: a hop that releases the whole body in ONE write makes the number of rendered states a function of the browser commit schedule rather than of the server (measured 2 on GoTavern and 1 on pinned, run 40299346339), so that mode was deleted and its claim is NOT made. Status stays PARTIAL on the two surviving gaps below -- the TLS-close gap and the absent ordering gate -- not on inertia: the network half is proven, the row is not. RE-DERIVED 2026-10-29: the two remaining gaps are closed by committed tests (a graceful TLS shutdown mid-frame, and the frame-ORDER property for a complete and a cancelled stream), and the row's browser instrumentation was already green and gate-checked, so the row carries no evidence gap and is PASS rather than PARTIAL. The buffering-proxy mode stays a DECIDED EXCLUSION in this row's notes, which is a decision and not a gap. CLOSURE RECORD (kept out of evidenceGap because a PASS row may not carry gaps): CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- MID-STREAM TLS CLOSE. The row said the fault 'is a socket close on plain HTTP' and that a TLS fatal alert was not reproduced; the first half was STALE (TestProductionTransportSurfacesAMidStreamCloseCausally already starts a TLS server and hijacks the connection), and the second half is now covered in BOTH directions: an ABRUPT close (existing test) and a GRACEFUL TLS shutdown mid-frame, where the server hijacks its `*tls.Conn` and closes it properly so a close_notify goes out. `TestProductionTransportTreatsAGracefulTLSShutdownMidStreamAsTruncation` requires that case to reach the caller as an ERROR (a silent success would show half an answer as a complete one), that the bytes that DID arrive are still delivered, that the error is classifiable (unexpected EOF / truncation / closed / reset) and that it carries no credential. Teeth observed: returning `io.EOF` instead of the mid-stream error turns it red with 'a provider that shut the TLS session down mid-frame produced NO error' CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- THE ORDERING PROPERTY, ASSERTED AS A PROPERTY RATHER THAN AS A RECORDED PARTIAL TEXT. `TestProductionTransportPreservesProviderFrameOrder` makes a provider write 200 distinguishable SSE frames one per write, with a flush after each so they arrive in separate reads, then requires the received bytes to equal the sent bytes AND the parsed frame indices to be 0..199 in order with none dropped or duplicated. Teeth observed: `count = count/2` in the stream reader turns it red with 'the streamed bytes differ from what the provider wrote (sent 3290 bytes, received 1590, first difference at byte 7)'. `TestProductionTransportDeliversACancelledStreamAsAnOrderedPrefix` closes the CANCELLATION half of the same property: after a mid-stream cancel, the bytes the caller holds must be a PREFIX of what the provider wrote -- the beginning of the real answer, not a reshuffled fragment -- which is what makes a per-run 'partial text at the moment of abort' observation unnecessary for the ordering claim

Five routes answer for themselves with ZERO outbound requests -- /api/content/importURL for chub/janitorai/pygmalion/risu/perchance (content.go:171-174), /api/content/importUUID for a non-AICC shape (content_uuid.go:146-151), and /api/image-metadata when generation is unsupported (image_metadata_get.go:71-74) -- each answering 501 and returning before any download or fetch. The negative is established by three searches: ReverseProxy has 126 hits in internal/ and cmd/ and every one is the pinned provider setting reverse_proxy from the request body; handback|hand-back|upstreamNode|proxyTo returns two test filenames and no implementation; the 18 StatusNotImplemented answers are provider-branch 501s

DATA hand-back: the driver and its judge now EXIST (tests/browser/q21-data-handback.mjs drives BOTH directions; tests/oracle/q21/judge-handback.mjs names the rows each direction requires and refuses `match` on zero counts), but the claim was later judged in CI and PASSED: Browser differential 40977195387 printed `hand-back verdict: match` with both directions judged and every count non-zero (GoTavern 5/5, pinned 17/17). An earlier execution of the same judge failed on pinnedContinued's persistence wait and passed on re-run, so the probe now records the page and chat-file tails on a timeout. The claim's live state is docs/goal-scorecard.md Q21
rows.notes: A backup nobody has restored is a file, not a backup. TWO OF THIS ROW S GAPS CLOSED 2026-10-29 by one committed test: the per-route 501 table (status + zero outbound per provider branch) and the inherited substring classifier (the chub look-alike is accepted, with a 404 control proving the assertion is discriminating). The row stays PARTIAL for the gaps that remain: no restore-into-a-tree test, and the REQUEST hand-back to Node is a recorded absence. CLOSED GAPS, moved out of evidenceGap so that field contains only OPEN gaps: CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- THE INHERITED CLASSIFIER IS NOW PINNED BY A TEST, not only recorded. The same table includes `https://chub.ai.attacker.example/...` and requires it to answer 501 (the chub branch's unimplemented status), because pinned classifies with `host.includes('chub.ai')` (AGENTS.md architecture boundary 5). A 404 there would have meant we had silently hardened a classifier and changed the compatibility claim; a weaker test would not have discriminated 'treated as chub' from 'refused by the whitelist', so the row's control (a genuinely unlisted host answering 404) sits beside it CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- THE PER-ROUTE 501 TABLE IS NOW ASSERTED, not read. `TestContentImportURLProviderBranchesAnswer501WithNoOutbound` drives `/api/content/importURL` for every provider host (chub.ai, characterhub.org, janitorai, pygmalion.chat, realm.risuai.net, perchance.org) plus a policy-refusal control, and pins BOTH halves of each branch: the STATUS (501 for not-implemented, 404 for the whitelist refusal, so the two stay distinguishable per AGENTS.md rule 17) and ZERO OUTBOUND REQUESTS, with a recording peer behind the seam so a branch that fetched before refusing would be visible as an arrival rather than as plausible data. Teeth observed: making the provider branches answer 404 turns the chub subtest red with 'POST /api/content/importURL https://chub.ai/characters/someone/a-character = 404, want 501' CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- RESTORE, driven the way the pinned UI drives it. `TestChatBackupRestoreRoundTripPreservesTheChat` performs the two client-side steps of `public/scripts/chat-backups.js:73-118` against one tree: it plants a character chat and the `chat_`-prefixed backup pinned would have left, DELETES the chat, downloads the backup through `POST /api/backups/chat/download` (asserting byte equality and the Content-Disposition the browser needs), then imports those bytes through `POST /api/chats/import` with the pinned multipart field names, and asserts the restored chat file carries the backup s MESSAGES in order. Teeth observed: making the import keep only the header line turns it red with "the restored chat s messages differ from the backup s: backup [Hello there. Hi Seraphina.] restored []". The ranked gap list entry for this row was re-derived: restore is closed, so the ranked item is now the REQUEST hand-back absence.

rows.area: Startup: config creation and migration, data seeding, locking, no-hang, no egress

wouldGoRedIfWrong.explanation: A boot over a stock layout that hangs fails this test inside startBounded's bound, printing the bound, the tree diff and the goroutine stacks. It is the row's own gate for P0-B and it exists at HEAD; the row previously claimed no gate existed, which is why the status was FAIL and is now PARTIAL.

evidenceGap: STARTUP-DIFFERENTIAL FIXTURES STILL START FROM FRESH OR MIGRATED RUNTIME ROOTS, never from a populated stock SillyTavern tree. A populated tree IS covered by two other gates -- `tests/e2e/longlived_test.go` synthesises one in Go and the packaged drop-in qualification boots an archive against a stock tree -- but neither is a startup-differential fixture, so the startup surface’s own corpus does not include one
rows.notes: RE-DERIVED 2026-10-29. The row was FAIL on a premise that is false at HEAD: it said no bounded-boot gate existed, and internal/app/startup_p0b_test.go has seven such gates, all passing, all through startBounded. One gap is real and remains: the startup-differential fixtures still begin from fresh or migrated roots rather than a populated stock tree (a populated tree is covered by the longlived e2e leg and the packaged drop-in gate, not by a startup fixture). The egress half of this row is CLOSED and is recorded below. The duplicate-key divergence recorded here is closed and gated at both the config layer and the shipped binary. CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- P0-B's bounded-boot gate NOW EXISTS and passes: internal/app/startup_p0b_test.go drives a stock tree in the working directory (`TestP0BStockTreeInWorkingDirectoryStarts`), a foreign working directory on a fresh tree (`TestP0BForeignWorkingDirectoryStartsOnAFreshTree`, which also asserts nothing is left in the launch directory), a config lock held by another process (`TestP0BConfigLockHeldByAnotherProcessFailsWithNamedError`), a stale lock file (`TestP0BStaleConfigLockFileDoesNotBlockBoot`), legacy keys (`TestP0BLegacyKeysBootBounded`) and two concurrent boots (`TestP0BTwoConcurrentBootsDoNotHang`). Every one goes through `startBounded`, whose failure names the bound, the tree changes and the goroutine stacks -- so a hang goes red with the wait named, which is what this row asked for. The earlier text claiming no such gate existed was STALE and is corrected here rather than kept CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- STARTUP EGRESS (AGENTS.md 25): the clause that stood in evidenceGap saying "NO GATE ASSERTS THAT STARTUP MAKES NO NON-ESSENTIAL NETWORK ACCESS" was STALE. `internal/app/startup_egress_test.go` runs the REAL boot under a recording resolver and asserts `TestStartupMakesNoEgressOnAFreshBoot`, `TestStartupDockerBranchResolvesExactlyTheAllowedHostnames`, `TestStartupDockerBranchWhitelistsTheAddressItResolved` and `TestStartupDockerHostnameLookupIsBounded`; because a resolver peer cannot see an IP literal, a subprocess or a hand-built resolver, `internal/app/startup_egress_source_test.go` adds the AST second opinion `TestStartupSourcesAddNoEgressPath` plus `TestEgressSourceScanHasTeeth` for the scan itself. The runtime observation stays primary and the source scan is beside it, never in place of it (AGENTS.md 54), and both are cited in evidence.tests. CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- DUPLICATE-KEY CONFIG: CLOSED 2026-10-29. pinned refuses it by name and does NOT rewrite the file (measured, tests/oracle/sillytavern-1.19.0-config-duplicate-key.json: exit 1, the yaml message with code DUPLICATE_KEY, then 'FATAL: Failed to read config.yaml. Please check the file for syntax errors.', and the config's bytes and mtime IDENTICAL before and after; the control -- the same document minus the duplicate -- boots AND is migrated 25 -> 3310 bytes). GoTavern used to ACCEPT a duplicate key, a divergence in the permissive direction; it now reproduces the refusal, asserted twice: `TestDuplicateKeyIsRejectedAsPinnedRecords` replays the recording against the config layer (exact message including the trimmed source frame and the duplicate's line/column, unchanged sha256, control migrated) and `TestDuplicateKeyConfigExitsOneWithPinnedLines` runs the shipped binary and asserts exit 1, the recorded stderr ORDER, the absence of a 'gotavern:' prefix or a fake Node stack, and an untouched file

rows.area: Release artifact: archive, install, upgrade, rollback, docker, smoke

evidence.releaseArtifact: release-qualification.yml extracts the archive, boots it over a fresh root, boots it a second time to assert idempotence, and exercises upgrade plus rollback; release-qualification.yml#qualify-dropin-linux and dropin-qualification.yml#dropin-current-head unpack an archive into a STOCK SillyTavern tree and boot it there (both layouts and both config modes, see docs/dropin-qualification.md)

wouldGoRedIfWrong.explanation: the row's claims about release artifact: archive, install, upgrade, rollback, docker, smoke rest on this test; deleting or weakening it makes the row unsupported, and the checker fails a row whose named test does not exist

evidenceGap: the stock-tree qualification executes the LINUX archive on every push (dropin-qualification.yml#dropin-current-head) and the WINDOWS archive on windows-latest (dropin-qualification.yml runs-on windows-latest: a Start.cmd run, a pristine-config run, a trimmed-config run and an exe-direct scenario) -- the older clause saying the Windows archive is never executed was stale and is removed

the stock tree the Linux job boots is DERIVED from the pinned source rather than recorded from a pinned Node run, so AGENTS.md 38's "the real migration path" is covered by a derivation, not by a captured tree

no qualification result for handing the data back to pinned Node AFTER GoTavern has run over it (AGENTS.md 38). The driver and its judge EXIST and PASSED in the browser-differential job (run 40977195387, hand-back verdict match, both directions, GoTavern 5/5 and pinned 17/17), so the capability is proven; what is missing is its PLACEMENT in the packaged drop-in gate. Moving it there is blocked on two concrete things, both named rather than implied: (a) the probe's spawn sites (tests/browser/q21-data-handback.mjs:637 and :917) do not pass `--browserLaunchEnabled false`, so a local run of it asks the product to open the operator's default browser, and the probe re-seeds its own config so a workflow-level pre-seed would be overwritten -- a probe-owner change; (b) dropin-qualification.yml would need the pinned checkout, the browser harness (`npm ci` in tests/browser), Playwright and `GOTAVERN_BINARY` wired into `dropin-current-head`; the exact proposed diff is in the Beta 1 compat lane report, not applied because `.github/workflows/**` is outside that lane.
quoted releaseArtifact here is a workflow step, not a recorded run id; the run id belongs in docs/goal-scorecard.md Q1/Q21
rows.notes: This row is the strongest release evidence in the tree, and its shape is now split in two: the release pipeline (archive, install into a fresh prefix, upgrade, rollback, docker) is exercised by release-qualification.yml, release-install-smoke.yml and docker.yml, and the drop-in promise (a stock tree, unpacked archive, existing config and data) by qualify-dropin-linux and by dropin-qualification.yml on every push to main. What is still missing is the platform and tree half named in evidenceGap: only the Linux archive is ever executed, and the stock tree is derived from the pinned source rather than recorded from a pinned Node run.

rows.area: Whole-session differential in a stock tree (load, settings, characters, chat, send, stream, save, reload)

wouldGoRedIfWrong.explanation: the gate is the committed harness pair plus its self-test: compare-whole-session-legs.mjs carries 39 required guards over the browser-observable, provider-wire and disk-state facts across all four legs (drive and restart on both subjects), and whole-session-gate-selftest.mjs mutates the run own four legs to produce 11/11 NAMED reds on an otherwise green baseline, so a comparator that stopped discriminating fails here instead of passing. Run 41171620691 at 91e1e15: verdict match, 39 guard(s), 0 failed, self-test 11/11 named mutations; the citation is a committed Node harness because this is a browser-only row and check.mjs records that citation vocabulary explicitly.

rows.notes: MEASURED, GATED AND GREEN: one stock tree per subject, one browser lineage over that tree, then a SERVER RESTART as a second process over the same tree; the comparator holds every browser-observable, disk-state and restart guard on both subjects. The measured cause of the original FAIL, in one verifiable sentence: the FAIL was a FIXTURE that compared an unsupported install shape (a binary without the release archive's `src/tokenizers` tree) against a supported one, so `/api/tokenizers` answered the pinned Guesstimate fallback (755 vs 589 and 971 vs 749) and the world-info token budget dropped the `power` entry (6682 B vs 7404 B); with the tokenizer tree installed beside the binary both subjects send the SAME 7404 B body (sha256 b0935add2892564da7f254ab54a2007a8329499db9bd0a5afb808cdea406bd4b) and the probe asserts `subject-tokenizes-exactly` on BOTH subjects (pinned must carry no exactness header, GoTavern must be exact on every tokenizer response). The product assembly was never the difference; the harness fix is 712f5f0 (it also fixes a measured first-send race by waiting for the chat to load). The gate was NEVER GREEN before this fix. CLOSURE RECORD: GoTavern whole-session differential 41171620691 at head 91e1e15 (success) is the run that closed this gap: four legs green (drive 27/27 and restart 12/12 on both subjects), comparator verdict match -- "whole-session: match -- 39 guard(s), 0 failed" (failedGuards: []), gate selftest 11/11 mutations produced their NAMED red, baseline green. The release gate re-runs this workflow at the final candidate SHA; that run is cited in the release record (docs/release-checklist.md and the GitHub Release), NOT here, because a citation inside this row cannot name a run of the commit that contains the row. LIMITS, printed by the comparator itself and not claimed: a real provider (the peer answers with markers), group chats, branches/checkpoints, multi-user trees, and every clock-bearing field (chat_metadata and per-message send_date are recorded and never compared).

session.purpose: The whole-session differential AGENTS.md 34/38 asks for EXISTS and is GREEN: one stock tree per subject, one browser lineage, then a server restart over the same tree, judged by a 39-guard comparator whose red was observed on a real first-turn difference before the fix (a harness installation defect - a missing tokenizer tree - not a product difference). The step table below is the PREVIOUS per-surface inventory that the shared session subsumes; those probes remain each surface's own evidence and are not replaced by the session leg. `sharedFixture` is true because the shared-session surface now exists and is green; `tools/compat-matrix/check.mjs` refuses sharedFixture=true beside a FAIL row, and that consistency is what this flip restores.

steps.userAction: open the pinned frontend root in a browser
open a chat and see its history
send a message and receive a completion
send with streaming on, then cancel mid-stream
reload the page and see the conversation back
steps.notImplemented: no probe reads state back through the frontend after a reload; chats-save-get compares the HTTP round trip, not the browser's rehydration

canonicalisation.method: Each step's observation is compared after replacing those four classes with markers by FIELD PATH, never by regex over the whole document, and the replacement is recorded beside the observation so it cannot be silently widened. Byte equality is never claimed for a field that carries a clock.
forbidden: sorting arrays whose order is the contract

gaps.title: An existing SillyTavern user’s tree is qualified through a DERIVED stock tree, and the hand-back after GoTavern has written the tree is not part of the drop-in gate
gaps.wouldStopARealUser: yes for an existing SillyTavern user, which is the entire target audience, until the stock tree is recorded from a pinned Node run and one full round trip returns the tree to pinned Node
gaps.evidence: row packaging-release: dropin-qualification.yml#dropin-current-head boots the Linux archive against a stock tree on every push, and #windows-inputs + #dropin-windows execute the WINDOWS archive on windows-latest (a Start.cmd run, a pristine-config run, a trimmed-config run and an exe-direct scenario); both layouts and both config modes are covered.
